title: Community-Anchored Proof
subtitle: Choosing the first zero-knowledge use case to implement against DTG credentials — and what any implementation of it must satisfy.
author: Glenn Gore (stormer78), First Person Project
audience: Four working groups: DTG Credentials · ZKP · Trust Registry · Governance

source.named: zkp-tf #18 — ScottJeezey 2026-08-27: 'a natural first one to seed it with'
source.note: Clause texts below are close paraphrases for crosswalk purposes; the record of authority is Glenn's document. The ADR is deliberately format-agnostic and 'does not choose how to build it' — the construction record is the how.

decision: The first zero-knowledge proof implemented against DTG credentials is the Community-Anchored Proof the Credentials Core Specification already describes: a relationship exists inside a shared community, without revealing who is in it.
whyThisOne: small enough to build, specific enough that succeeding proves something real
already described in the specification — implementing it is conformance, not invention
cannot be quietly satisfied by disclosing fewer fields: clause 3 is a statement about someone else's credential
statement: A member of community C has a working relationship with me, and I am also a member of community C.

mustProve.text: the holder possesses a valid relationship credential
the holder possesses a valid membership credential from community C

the party who issued that relationship credential also holds a valid membership credential from the same community C — 'the hard one': a statement about someone else's credential, proven without the other party online, asked, or aware

clauses.text: reveals no relationship identifier from the relationship credential
reveals no identifier of the counterparty who issued it
reveals no identifier of the holder beyond attributes the holder deliberately discloses
two proofs from the same credentials cannot be linked — by one verifier or by verifiers comparing notes
clauses.refinement: full show-unlinkability cannot coexist with reuse detection in the same context (ePrint 2026/333 §5.3); parameterise by context: unlinkable across contexts, the declared nullifier the only link within a reuse-detecting one

clauses.text: a verifier learns the outcome and deliberately disclosed attributes, nothing further
a party lacking the required credentials cannot produce a verifying proof
clause 3 cannot be satisfied unless the counterparty genuinely holds a membership credential from the same community
clauses.boundTo: 010 method (set-membership on the voucher's grant leaf, card 001)
clauses.refinement: proves the community-issued grant half only (cred-spec PR #12 pair; PR #26 carve-out) — the acknowledgement is not in the presenter's hands

clauses.text: the counterparty need not be online, consulted, or aware
clauses.boundTo: 010 witness (proven from root_C, not from the voucher)
clauses.refinement: under WD02 pairwise identifiers the voucher's linkage (VRC-side ↔ VMC-side identifier) must have been supplied at issuance or avoided by one directed identifier — card 007 / HR-2; otherwise clause 3 is unprovable offline

clauses.text: the presenter proves they are the subject of the credentials, not merely a holder of copies
bound to a verifier challenge; not replayable to another verifier or time
(added by the ZKP TF) the voucher is not the holder — a self-vouch is unsatisfiable
clauses.refinement: without it a member with two identifiers vouches for themselves and clauses 1–3 verify

clauses.text: (added, WD02) the identifiers a party used in the VRC and in their VMC are controlled by one secret
clauses.refinement: cred-spec PR #30 §Community-Anchored: 'the proof must additionally establish common control'

clauses.text: does not verify if any relied-on credential is revoked or suspended
states the registry state it was made against; the verifier judges recency
establishing currency must not itself identify the holder
clauses.refinement: holds only if roots are fetched without a per-holder query — stated as the condition

clauses.text: the delay between a change and proofs reflecting it is bounded and published
clauses.refinement: the bound is a registry/governance publication, not a proof property — construction carries it as a horizon input

clauses.text: a verifier confirms the community is one it recognises without learning which member
clauses.boundTo: 010 public inputs (root_C at a stated registry state)

clauses.text: whatever the proof relies on from a registry is independently checkable by a party that did not create it
clauses.boundTo: 006 set-root primitive route · public inputs set roots
clauses.refinement: the set-root primitive (cred-tf #40): signed published root + zero-knowledge membership/status proof in the presentation; paths and openings stay private; root/witness retrieval requires an explicit privacy policy

clauses.text: two verifiers checking against the same registry state reach the same verdict
a registry's obligations are stated as an interface so any conformant registry can serve these proofs
proving is feasible on the devices that hold credentials — a phone or an agent — within a stated time and memory budget
clauses.boundTo: 010 substitutions (Groth16 est. ≈35–45k constraints ~2 s; blackbox 0.03 s/vouch) · stacks layer (ProveKit phone numbers)
clauses.refinement: budgets not yet stated by the TF; the options layer supplies measured numbers per stack for the gate to set them

clauses.text: verification is cheap enough to run inline
a proof fits the transports DTG credentials already travel over
clauses.boundTo: stacks layer: proof size column (721 B Groth16 vs ~716 KB WHIR)
clauses.refinement: a profile decision; the options table shows both numbers

clauses.text: published test vectors covering proofs that must verify and proofs that must fail
clauses.boundTo: 010 conformance fixtures families · runtimes/fixtures format (accept/reject/lint vectors, rejection-reason register)
clauses.refinement: format exists and is consumed cross-language; 010's own vector family not yet cut

clauses.text: an independent implementation can verify another's proofs
clauses.refinement: reproduced for cards 001/002/003/005; 010 composition not yet built

clauses.text: any requirement on how credentials are issued is stated explicitly and early
clauses.boundTo: 010 issuance (ZK-friendly signature or published commitment; issuer linkage MAY) · cred-spec #17

clauses.text: a community declares whether private presentation is required, default, or optional
the assurance a proof carries is traceable to the governance of the issuing community
clauses.boundTo: 010 yield (assurance class via C's governance) · doesNotEstablish (admission correctness)

acceptanceTests.name: Accepts
acceptanceTests.text: a valid proof verifies and a written analysis shows the verifier learned the outcome and nothing more

acceptanceTests.name: Rejects
acceptanceTests.text: with the voucher not a member of C the proof cannot be produced or does not verify — clause 3 does real work
acceptanceTests.family: rejects-unsat / rejects-verify (the construction distinguishes the two)

acceptanceTests.name: Unlinkable
acceptanceTests.text: two proofs from the same credentials given to two verifiers who compare cannot be linked

acceptanceTests.name: Current
acceptanceTests.text: after the voucher's membership is revoked a proof relying on it stops verifying within the published bound

outOfScope: the construction — how the three clauses combine into one proof (the construction record's method)
how a registry publishes what proofs rely on (the set-root primitive is one answer)
delegation chains — 'the natural next case' → construction 020

workingGroupAsks.DTG Credentials: confirm the three clauses match the specified Community-Anchored Proof; identify issuance requirements
workingGroupAsks.ZKP: choose the construction, build a reference prover and verifier, publish X1/X2 vectors
workingGroupAsks.Trust Registry: define what a registry exposes for a proof to rely on; how currency and revocation are expressed
workingGroupAsks.Governance: how a community declares private presentation policy; how assurance traces to governance

consequencesNamed: requirements on issuance reach every issuer — hence X3 early
registries gain a new obligation; revocation must be rethought so currency checks do not undo privacy
real cost on holder devices — hence D1
a harder first milestone by intent

crosswalkSummary.note: counts include S6/S7 (added by the TF); 26 original clauses + 4 acceptance tests + the 3 must-prove clauses are the record's testable content
